title: Implement rate-credit ledger + usage fingerprint debugger to resolve cross-shard quota drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see subtle per-model quota drift and reconciliation gaps when requests are rate-limited and later retried/backfilled. Root causes we've observed in recent incidents include: (1) refunded tokens not being consistently recorded across ingest shards, (2) idempotency token collisions producing double-credits, and (3) late-event backfills not mapping to the same aggregation key used by real-time rate-limit tallies. The symptom is console charts showing under/over allocation for specific models and transient quota anomalies for customers on Dedicated.

Proposed solution: Build a small persistent 'rate-credit ledger' service that records every credit/debit (token consumption, prefix-kv cache hits, rate-limit refunds) with a compact usage fingerprint that ties events across ingestion paths. Combine that with a developer-facing 'usage fingerprint debugger' in the Console (read-only) which allows SRE/PM/Support to search by request id, idempotency token, or time window and see the ledger trail and derived per-model tallies. The ledger is append-only, sharded by customer_id and day, and emits materialized deltas used by both backfill reconciler and live aggregator to ensure the same source-of-truth for quota accounting.

Goals:
- Prevent recurring per-model drift caused by mismatched aggregation keys
- Make rate-limit refunds auditable and reconstructable
- Give support engineers a fast debug path to explain console discrepancies to customers

Out of scope: full migration of billing exporter, long-term retention tier, or changing public pricing mechanics. This ticket is about correctness and observability for usage accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger receives and stores token-level credit/debit events for 99% of live ingest paths in dev stack
Backfill reconciler consumes ledger deltas and produces identical per-model tallies to live aggregator within 1% for test workloads
Console debug UI surfaces ledger traces by request id/idempotency token with <3s query latency for 7d retention
Automated integration tests for retry/refund flows and idempotency collisions added to pipeline
tasks: Design ledger schema and compact usage fingerprint (Aisha)
Implement append-only ledger API + storage adapter (Marcus)
Instrument rate-limiter to emit refund events with ledger-safe keys (Tiffany)
Wire backfill reconciler to read ledger deltas (Data Eng)
Add Console read-only debug view and search panel (Frontend)
Add integration tests and canary traffic runbook (SRE)
implementation_notes: Ledger entries will be small newline-delimited JSON in storage with the following fields encoded in the fingerprint: customer_id, model_alias, ingestion_shard_id, sequence_epoch (hourly), idempotency_token_hash. We will use the existing blob-s3 pathing for append segments and a compact index in Redis for recent-day queries. The ledger is not intended to be a global SQL source for analytics; we will export compact deltas to the TSDB/warehouse for downstream charts.
risks_and_mitigation: Storage cost for high-volume customers — mitigate with per-customer sampling and 7d hot retention + cold archive
Index contention on Redis during bursts — mitigate by sharding index keys by (customer_id mod 256)
Query privacy/leak risk in Console — debug view is read-only and RBAC-gated; require SSO group for access
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger write/read semantics, property tests for idempotency hashing, end-to-end replay tests that compare backfill reconciler output vs live aggregator on synthetic traffic (100k requests/day scale). Add a canary where 5% of customer traffic is mirrored into ledger-first flow for 48 hours and monitor delta metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy ledger in dev and run integration suite. 2) Canary 5% mirror in staging for 48h (observe deltas). 3) Canary 5% production mirror (non-blocking) for 72h. 4) Flip replacer for reconciler to authoritative deltas for 10% customers. 5) Gradual ramp to 100% with runbook to revert to best-effort aggregator.
